newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL interbank rates steady in thin market.
newsitem.headline: KL interbank rates steady in thin market.

text.p: Interbank rates were mostly unchanged with the market relatively inactive due to the absence of many dealers and banks, dealers said on Thursday.
They said a holiday mood continued to prevail over the market after a five-day closure of banks from February 7 to 11 for the Chinese Lunar New Year and Moslem Eid al-Fitr.
They said the one-week interbank rate was at 7.45/55 percent, two-week was at 7.40/45 percent and one-month to six-month at 7.35/40 percent, all unchanged from Wednesday.

"The market should return to normal next week when everybody comes back to work and funds which had gone out during the festivals also return to the system," said the head of money dealing at a Malaysian bank.
He said interest rates were expected to ease slightly as funds return to the system over the next two weeks.
An estimated three billion ringgit has temporarily left the banking system, mostly in cash, for the festivals.
Dealers said the overnight rate was expected to remain steady between 7.0 and 8.0 percent over the next one week.
